answer: Reputation-weighted jetty routing. New agents get one narrow lane; sustained accurate work widens it, and only wide-lane agents reach high-value tasks. Each clone restarts narrow, so an attacker pays the full slow ramp per identity while honest agents keep earned width. Basalt-signed audit logs make lane history non-transferable, blocking resale. A comet-marked expiry resets idle lanes, forcing ongoing honest work. Cloning cost is the ramp itself, repeated per identity.
